---
name: data-coverage-quirks
description: cell_1/experiment1 responses.csv coverage gaps that limit which test statistics are computable
metadata:
  type: project
---
Found 2026-10-30 (iter_4 critique). responses.csv has 2250 rows and 172 sets, with about 5 answers per (set, target) cell and no participant_id.
- Power-of-2 sets never ask about a power-of-2 target that isn't an example, so you can't test "powers vs multiples" there directly. Use the multiples-of-4 yes rate (0.44) instead.
- Sets whose examples all share a last digit: targets with that last digit get 0.96 yes (n=55), other targets 0.06 (n=505).
- 92,82,27,42 and 22,62,26,82 get high yes rates across the 20s. 83,38,58,68 gets 85/87/89 yes and 50-76 no.

**Why:** saves re-checking coverage when designing statistics.
**How to apply:** check that a stimulus slice has targets before building a statistic on it. See [[exponent-concept-cost-finding]].
---
name: exponent-concept-cost-finding
description: Number-game data favour multiples-of-m over powers/squares/cubes; fitted extra prior cost on exponent concepts gained ~47 nats MAP over erlang_interval_simplicity_search
metadata:
  type: project
---
Round 3 (2026-10-30), cell_1/experiment1: adding a fitted extra log-prior cost on powers/squares/cubes to erlang_interval_simplicity_search raised MAP loglik from -873.7 to -826.3 (cost fit at about 5). Key items: 32,4,16→12 and 64,4→72 (people answer "multiples of 4"). Adding residue classes (x mod k = r) hurt by 20 nats (75,48,12,3 is ≡3 mod 9). Removing contains-digit rules hurt by 52. Submitted as `multiplicative_not_exponential_concepts`.

**Why:** saves re-running these concept-space screens.
**How to apply:** when MAP-screening, compile p_yes with `model.replace_rvs_by_values([model['p_yes']])[0]`. Otherwise compile_fn uses random RV draws and the per-trial predictions are garbage.
---
name: final-digit-salience-finding
description: Fitted log-prior bonus on "ends in d" rules gained ~38 nats MAP over erlang_interval_simplicity_search; many other tweaks gained ~0
metadata:
  type: project
---
Round 3 repair (2026-10-30), cell_1/experiment1: MAP screens on erlang_interval_simplicity_search (base loglik -873.7).
- Gained nothing (<0.1 nat): fitted stray-noise rate, separate size-principle weight, fitted Erlang shape, a decade-aligned interval bonus, a bonus on the full 1-100 range, a multiples-of-m bonus (which was rejected as a near-duplicate).
- Big gains: "ends in d" bonus alone gave -835.4 (bonus about 2.2, cost about 4.0). Separate ends and contains bonuses gave -826.9. One digit-rule bonus gave -852.3.
- The largest per-set misfits: 92,82,27,42 (it over-uses "contains 2"), 62,32,22 and 83,38,58,68 (it over-uses "even"), and the square/power sets (see [[exponent-concept-cost-finding]]).
Submitted as `final_digit_salient_concept_search`.

**Why:** saves re-screening dead-end tweaks.
**How to apply:** for this base model, change which rules are in the hypothesis space or how they are priced. Tweaks to the likelihood, noise or interval prior do not move the fit.
---
name: incumbent-null-changes-round3
description: Changes to erlang_interval_simplicity_search that fit to ~0 at MAP (novelty-rejected risk) vs the digit-notation discount that gained ~21 nats
metadata:
  type: project
---
Round 3 (2026-10-30), cell_1/experiment1 MAP screens on erlang_interval_simplicity_search (baseline LL -873.7):
- divisibility salience bonus: fit ~0, rejected as near-duplicate (RMSE 0.0009).
- fitted stray rate: stays at 0.10, no gain. "Any number 1-100" concept: weight -> 0. Decade-aligned interval bonus: +1.5 only. Extra cost on contains-digit rules alone: +2.6.
- Separate fitted log-prior shift for all 20 digit-notation rules (ending-in/contains): -852.3 (+21), fits as a BONUS (~2) while primitive cost rises to ~4.6. Submitted as `notation_cheap_simplicity_search`. It makes shared-divisor under-extension worse (0.56 vs obs 0.71).

**Why:** a change whose parameter fits to ~0 gets rejected by the novelty gate.
**How to apply:** screen at MAP first, and only submit changes whose parameter moves away from its null. See [[exponent-concept-cost-finding]].
- [Exponent concept cost finding](exponent-concept-cost-finding.md) — powers/squares cost extra; MAP-screen tips
- [Incumbent null changes round 3](incumbent-null-changes-round3.md) — which refinements fit to ~0; digit-notation discount gained 21
- [Final-digit salience finding](final-digit-salience-finding.md) — ends-in-d bonus +38 nats; noise/gamma/shape/decade tweaks gave nothing
- [Data coverage quirks](data-coverage-quirks.md) — no power targets in power sets; shared-last-digit yes 0.96

"""Multiplicative, not exponential, concept space.

People's concept space for numbers is built on multiplication, not
exponentiation: they readily entertain parity, "multiples of m", final digits,
digits contained and numerical ranges, but concepts that require repeated
multiplication -- powers of a base, perfect squares, perfect cubes -- are a
priori much less accessible, carrying a fitted extra cost on top of the
ordinary per-primitive simplicity cost, size principle and near-all-or-none
commitment. So after 32, 4, 16 or 4, 64 people generalise to other multiples of
4 rather than restricting themselves to powers of 2 or 4.

Built on erlang_interval_simplicity_search (complexity-costed rules, Erlang
prior on interval size); the one change is the fitted log-prior cost on the
exponentiation-based concepts.
"""
import numpy as np
import pymc as pm
import pytensor.tensor as pt

N = 100
NUMS = np.arange(1, N + 1)


def _rules():
    # Each rule with its description length and whether it needs exponentiation.
    r, c, e = [NUMS % 2 == 1, NUMS % 2 == 0], [1, 1], [0, 0]
    primes = np.array([n > 1 and all(n % d for d in range(2, int(n ** 0.5) + 1)) for n in NUMS])
    r.append(primes)
    r.append(np.isin(NUMS, [k * k for k in range(1, 11)]))
    r.append(np.isin(NUMS, [k ** 3 for k in range(1, 5)]))
    c += [2, 2, 2]
    e += [0, 1, 1]
    for b in range(2, 11):
        r.append(np.isin(NUMS, [b ** k for k in range(0, 8) if b ** k <= N]))
        c.append(2)
        e.append(1)
    p2 = [2 ** k for k in range(0, 7)]
    r.append(np.isin(NUMS, [x for x in p2 if x != 32]))
    r.append(np.isin(NUMS, p2 + [37]))
    c += [3, 3]
    e += [1, 1]
    for m in list(range(3, 10)) + [11, 12]:
        r.append(NUMS % m == 0)
        c.append(2)
        e.append(0)
    for d in range(10):
        r.append(NUMS % 10 == d)
        c.append(2)
        e.append(0)
    for d in range(10):
        r.append(np.array([str(d) in str(n) for n in NUMS]))
        c.append(2)
        e.append(0)
    return np.array(r, dtype=float), np.array(c, dtype=float), np.array(e, dtype=float)


RULES, RULE_COST, IS_EXP = _rules()
_iv = [(a, b) for a in range(1, N + 1) for b in range(a, N + 1)]
INTERVALS = np.array([(NUMS >= a) & (NUMS <= b) for a, b in _iv], dtype=float)
MEMBER = np.vstack([RULES, INTERVALS])  # H x 100
SIZES = MEMBER.sum(1)
INT_SIZES = INTERVALS.sum(1)
LOG_INT_SIZES = np.log(INT_SIZES)
NOISE = 0.1


def prepare_observed(rows):
    sets = []
    idx = {}
    set_i, tgt = [], []
    for r in rows:
        s = str(r["number_set"]).strip()
        if s not in idx:
            idx[s] = len(sets)
            sets.append([int(x) for x in s.split(",")])
        set_i.append(idx[s])
        tgt.append(int(float(r["target"])) - 1)
    loglik = np.zeros((len(sets), MEMBER.shape[0]))
    for i, ex in enumerate(sets):
        for x in ex:
            pin = MEMBER[:, x - 1] * (1 - NOISE) / SIZES
            loglik[i] += np.log(pin + NOISE / N)
    return {
        "set_loglik": loglik,
        "set_idx": np.array(set_i, dtype="int64"),
        "target_idx": np.array(tgt, dtype="int64"),
        "rating": np.array([int(float(r["rating"])) for r in rows], dtype="int64"),
    }


with pm.Model() as model:
    set_loglik = pm.Data("set_loglik", np.zeros((1, MEMBER.shape[0])))
    set_idx = pm.Data("set_idx", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))
    target_idx = pm.Data("target_idx", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))

    lam = pm.Beta("lambda_rules", 2.0, 2.0)  # prior mass on rules vs intervals
    cost = pm.HalfNormal("primitive_cost", sigma=5.0)  # log-prior cost per extra primitive
    exp_cost = pm.Normal("exponent_cost", 0.0, 3.0)  # extra log-prior cost of power/square/cube concepts
    log_beta = pm.Normal("log_beta", 0.5, 1.0)  # commitment exponent (log scale)
    beta = pm.Deterministic("beta", pt.exp(log_beta))
    lapse = pm.Beta("lapse", 1.0, 10.0)
    log_sigma = pm.Normal("log_sigma", np.log(20.0), 1.0)  # Erlang scale of interval size
    sigma = pm.Deterministic("sigma", pt.exp(log_sigma))

    rule_logp = -cost * (RULE_COST - 1.0) - exp_cost * IS_EXP
    rule_logp = rule_logp - pt.logsumexp(rule_logp)  # normalised within rules
    int_logp = LOG_INT_SIZES - INT_SIZES / sigma
    int_logp = int_logp - pt.logsumexp(int_logp)  # normalised within intervals
    log_prior = pt.concatenate([pt.log(lam) + rule_logp, pt.log1p(-lam) + int_logp])
    logpost = beta * (set_loglik + log_prior[None, :])
    w = pt.special.softmax(logpost, axis=1)  # S x H
    p_in = pt.dot(w, pt.as_tensor_variable(MEMBER))  # S x 100
    p_raw = p_in[set_idx, target_idx]
    p_yes = pm.Deterministic(
        "p_yes", pt.clip(lapse * 0.5 + (1 - lapse) * p_raw, 1e-6, 1 - 1e-6)
    )

    rating = pm.Data("rating", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))
    pm.Bernoulli("response", p=p_yes, observed=rating)

import sys, csv, importlib.util, numpy as np, pymc as pm
from scipy.optimize import minimize
spec=importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("m", sys.argv[1]); m=importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)
rows=list(csv.DictReader(open('responses.csv')))
obs=m.prepare_observed(rows)
with m.model:
    pm.set_data(obs)
mod=m.model
vv=mod.value_vars
ll=mod.compile_fn(mod.observedlogp if hasattr(mod,'observedlogp') else mod.logp(vars=mod.observed_RVs),inputs=vv,on_unused_input='ignore')
lp=mod.compile_fn(mod.logp(),inputs=vv)
ip=mod.initial_point()
shapes=[(v.name,np.shape(ip[v.name])) for v in vv]
def unpack(x):
    d={};i=0
    for n,s in shapes:
        k=int(np.prod(s)); d[n]=x[i:i+k].reshape(s); i+=k
    return d
x0=np.concatenate([np.ravel(ip[n]) for n,_ in shapes])
best=None
rng=np.random.default_rng(0)
for t in range(8):
    x=x0+rng.normal(0,1,len(x0))*(t>0)
    r=minimize(lambda z:-lp(unpack(z)),x,method='Nelder-Mead',options={'maxiter':4000,'xatol':1e-4,'fatol':1e-4})
    if best is None or r.fun<best.fun: best=r
d=unpack(best.x); print({k:np.round(v,3) for k,v in d.items()}); print('loglik',ll(d))
import collections
pf=mod.compile_fn(mod.replace_rvs_by_values([mod['p_yes']])[0],inputs=vv,on_unused_input='ignore'); py=pf(d); np.save(sys.argv[1]+".npy",py)
agg=collections.defaultdict(lambda:[0,0,0])
for r,p in zip(rows,py):
    ex=[int(x) for x in r['number_set'].split(',')]; t=int(r['target'])
    if len(ex)<2 or t in ex: continue
    if any(all(e%mm==0 for e in ex) and t%mm==0 for mm in range(3,11)):
        a=agg[(r['number_set'],t)]; a[0]+=int(r['rating']); a[1]+=p; a[2]+=1
O=sum(a[0] for a in agg.values());P=sum(a[1] for a in agg.values());N=sum(a[2] for a in agg.values()); print('stat',O/N,P/N)
for k,(o,p,n) in agg.items():
    if abs(o/n-p/n)>0.3: print(k, o/n, round(p/n,2))
('20,32,92', 64) 1.0 0.57
('20,32,92', 56) 1.0 0.58
('33,3', 87) 0.0 0.38
('32,4,16', 12) 1.0 0.18
('64,4', 72) 0.6 0.16

cat << 'EOF' > $D/hypothesis.md
People's number concepts are built from multiplication (parity, multiples of m, final digits, ranges, with powers/squares/cubes costing extra), but a digit buried anywhere inside a numeral is hard to notice as the basis of a rule: concepts of the form "contains the digit d" carry a fitted extra prior cost over other rules of the same length. So when all examples happen to contain a 2 (e.g. 92, 82, 27, 42), people read them as "ends in 2" with a stray, or as a range, rather than "contains a 2", and say no to targets like 23 or 52's neighbours that share a contained digit but not a final digit.
EOF

python3 - <<EOF
src=open('$D/scratch/vB.py').read()
i=src.index('"""',3)+3
doc='''"""Hidden-digit concepts are costly.

People's number concepts are built from multiplication (parity, multiples of
m, final digits, ranges, with powers/squares/cubes costing extra), but a digit
buried anywhere inside a numeral is hard to notice as the basis of a rule:
concepts of the form "contains the digit d" carry a fitted extra prior cost
over other rules of the same length. So when all examples contain a 2
(92, 82, 27, 42), people read them as "ends in 2" with a stray, or as a range,
rather than "contains a 2", and reject targets that share a contained digit
but not a final digit.

Built on multiplicative_not_exponential_concepts (complexity-costed rules,
exponent cost, Erlang interval prior); the one change is the fitted log-prior
cost on contains-digit concepts (IS_EXP == 2 marks them).
"""'''
src=doc+src[i:]
src=src.replace('cc = pm.Normal("cc", 0.0, 3.0)','contains_cost = pm.Normal("contains_digit_cost", 0.0, 3.0)  # extra log-prior cost of contains-digit concepts').replace('- cc * (IS_EXP == 2)','- contains_cost * (IS_EXP == 2)')

Round 4 (2026-10-30), cell_1/experiment1: MAP screens on multiplicative_not_exponential_concepts (base loglik -826.3).

content.content: People's number concepts are built from multiplication (parity, multiples of m, final digits, ranges, with powers/squares/cubes costing extra), but a digit buried anywhere inside a numeral is hard to notice as the basis of a rule: concepts of the form "contains the digit d" carry a fitted extra prior cost over other rules of the same length. So when all examples happen to contain a 2 (e.g. 92, 82, 27, 42), people read them as "ends in 2" with a stray, or as a range, rather than "contains a 2", and say no to targets such as 23 or 25 that share a contained digit but not a final digit.

content.text:
I wrote the candidate as **`hidden_digit_costly_concepts`**, and it passes the admission check (`OK`). That check doesn't test whether it's too similar to existing models, and a single 100-draw chain can't confirm convergence.

**Hypothesis:** People build number rules from multiplication-based concepts, as in the current best model. The one change is that a digit sitting anywhere inside a number is hard to notice as the basis of a rule. So "contains the digit d" rules pay an extra prior cost, fitted from the data. For example, after 92, 82, 27, 42, people read "ends in 2" with one stray, or a range, rather than "contains a 2". This targets the critique's strongest finding, which survives the false-discovery correction: people say yes to targets that share a contained digit but not a final digit 43% of the time, while the best model predicts 61%.

**Quick best-fit screens against the current best model:**

| Variant | Fit (log-likelihood) |
|---|---|
| Current best model | −826.3 |
| Extra cost on contains-digit rules (submitted) | −809.4, about 17 nats better; the cost fits at about 1.5 |
| "Tens digit is d" rules in place of contains-digit rules | −868.5, much worse, so dropped |

The fitted cost sits well away from zero, so the model shouldn't be rejected as a near-duplicate of the best one.

**Closest existing model:** `notation_cheap_simplicity_search` also re-prices digit rules. But it moved "ends in d" and "contains d" together, on an older base model, and it lost. This one charges only the contains-digit rules, on top of the current best model.

The smoke fit took 116 seconds and gave a log-likelihood of −812.2. I also saved the screen results to the agent notes.

Files are in `_runs/cell_1/experiment1/model_loop/iter_4/candidate_1/`:
- `hypothesis.md`
- `model_name.txt`
- `candidate.py`
